result.title: Beyond What They Say: Cue Acknowledgment and Robustness in Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Explanations are used to assess whether vision-language models rely on visual evidence or misleading suggestions. A response that explicitly names a cue can still follow it, making disclosure alone an incomplete basis for judging robustness. We ask whether greater cue acknowledgment accompanies greater resistance. We compare matched answers and explanations under helpful, misleading, and conflicting visual and textual cues while holding the underlying question and correct answer fixed. A paired comparison shows that a model can select the endorsed wrong answer more often while acknowledging the cues more often. Reduced silence therefore need not indicate improved resistance. Explanations may also mention a textual suggestion while omitting an accompanying visual cue. Requesting evidence and acknowledgment does not consistently improve resistance in the tested settings. Outcomes vary across models and settings, and these comparisons do not isolate a causal effect of acknowledgment. Evaluations should report cue following and acknowledgment on the same instances, distinguishing visual from textual cues.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究在固定问题与正确答案的条件下，比较视觉与文本线索在有用、误导、冲突三种情形下 VLM 的答案与解释，考察模型对线索的「承认」是否伴随对线索的抵抗。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接关涉 VLM 是否真正使用视觉证据，并揭示「说明中提及线索」与「答案是否被线索左右」的解耦，可为视觉证据筛选、latent 内容是否被答案使用的诊断与评价设计提供核查线索。
